issues.legal_issue: A person who remains in possession after termination of a tenancy remains protected as a tenant against execution of an eviction decree, including a decree entered by compromise, where the rent-control law covers continuing possession and restricts eviction under decrees.
material_facts: An advocate rented a building and agreed in a compromise to vacate it by a specified date; an eviction decree was entered on the compromise before the rent-control law was extended to the area.
The tenant remained continuously in possession after the decree and after the law’s extension.
The landlord did not establish a ground for eviction under the rent-control law.
The parties later agreed to a sale of the property, and the court recorded their agreement as an undertaking; it formally dismissed the appeal because no further relief was needed.
issues.conclusion: The tenant remained a tenant under the Act despite the compromise decree and continued to enjoy the protection of Section 13(1), so execution of the eviction decree could not proceed. The appeal was formally dismissed following the parties’ settlement.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(i) and 13(1) of the East Punjab Urban Rent Restriction Act, 1949, read together, include a former tenant who continues in possession and prohibit eviction in execution of a decree, whether passed before or after the Act’s commencement, except as the Act permits. The inclusive definition preserves statutory tenant status even if a decree or other process has ended the tenancy under general property law. The Act is beneficial legislation and should be construed liberally to fulfil its protective purpose; interpretative doubt favours the potential evictee unless the language plainly provides for eviction. Subudhi’s case, decided under the Orissa House-Rent Control Act, 1958, was distinguishable because that Act’s definition expressly excluded a person against whom an eviction decree had been made.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_execution and applicable_scheme_covers_eviction_decrees and tenant_definition_covers_continuing_possession and eviction_decree_exists and tenant_remains_in_possession and not statutory_eviction_ground_established

predicates.rent_control_eviction_execution: A proceeding seeks to execute a decree for eviction under a rent-control scheme.
predicates.applicable_scheme_covers_eviction_decree: The applicable scheme restricts eviction in execution of decrees, including decrees made before the scheme took effect.
predicates.tenant_definition_covers_continuing_poss: The applicable scheme defines a tenant to include a person who continues in possession after the tenancy ends.
predicates.eviction_decree_exists: A court has entered a decree for eviction against the occupier.
predicates.tenant_remains_in_possession: The occupier continues to possess the premises after the tenancy ends and the decree is entered.
predicates.statutory_eviction_ground_established: The landlord has established a ground for eviction permitted by the applicable scheme.

issues.definition: When an eviction decree is being executed under a rent-control scheme that covers decrees and treats a person continuing in possession as a tenant, execution is barred if the person remains in possession and no permitted eviction ground has been established.
